label: rem:skein-generation-hadron-reading
title: Fundamental knots, the Hopf link and the hadron reading of skein generation
html:
In the particle dictionary, a knot type is fundamental if it is the unknot or a torus knot: the unknot (neutrino), the trefoil 3_1, the cinquefoil 5_1 (tau) and the torus (p, 2) family. The electron is not among them: it is \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3, whose closure is the Hopf link, with the trefoil \sigma_0^3 \in B_2 kept as a backup candidate. Every fundamental knot has \mathrm{Vol}(K) = 0, but not conversely: satellite knots, including composites such as 3_1 \# 3_1, also have volume zero. The Hopf link \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}} is read as the binding operation, and a hadron H \in \mathrm{Sym}^n(K) \otimes \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}} as a configuration of fundamental knots joined by Hopf links.

13.4.9 resolves every such H to P_H(a, q)\,[U]. In particular the fundamental knots and the Hopf link generate the skein module, but so does the unknot alone, and the resolution records linking only through the polynomial P_H.

The mass reading takes the form \mathfrak{m}(H) = Q(q)\, \mathfrak{m}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}) + \sum_i \mathrm{Vol}(K_i)/\hbar_q^2 of 13.4.10, so that a hadron built from fundamental constituents takes its whole mass from linking. That step needs a specialisation in which the Hopf link is not identified with the unknot. The specialization a = q, where the skein relation reads q L_+ - q^{-1} L_- = (q - q^{-1}) L_0, forces P_L = 1 for every link and identifies the Hopf link with the unknot, so it does not supply that step. At a = 1 the Hopf link resolves to (q - q^{-1})\,[U] with the orientation for which its crossings are positive, and the split unlink to 0, so linking is visible there. Which specialisation the mass reading uses is not fixed by the proposition.
